response.outputText: {"title":"Testing for Dead: Verification Procedure","question":"Why must a voltage tester be proved on a known live source both immediately before and immediately after testing for dead at the point of work?","answers":[{"text":"Because a reading of zero on an unproved tester proves nothing, so proving confirms the tester is working correctly throughout the test","correct":true,"feedback":"Correct. The tester must be proved on a known live source immediately before and after the test, since an unproved tester showing zero gives no reliable evidence that the conductors are actually dead."},{"text":"Because the tester battery drains quickly and needs to be checked only at the end of the job","correct":false,"feedback":"The evidence does not mention battery drainage as the reason for proving; proving is about verifying the tester functions correctly before and after use, not about battery life."},{"text":"Because proving the tester once before testing is enough to guarantee accurate results for the rest of the shift","correct":false,"feedback":"This is incorrect because the tester must be proved both before and after the test, not just once before starting work for the day."},{"text":"Because the permit requires a signature from a supervisor confirming the tester was recently serviced","correct":false,"feedback":"The evidence describes proving the tester on a known live source, not obtaining a supervisor signature about servicing."}],"evidenceIds":["ev-s42","ev-s43","ev-s44","ev-s46","ev-s50"]}
